title: Google wants everyone to have their own AI-generated Truman Show
excerpt: A proposed TV lineup stitches crime capers, rom coms and sci fi into hyperpersonal episodes drawn from your data.
content_html:
Published Nov 24, 2026, 1:07 PM EST

Hamed holds a B.A. in English Literature, and graduated top of his class. He loves music, tech gadgets, and exploring the latest in the world of LLMs. He also enjoys tinkering with creative software such as Logic Pro, Final Cut Pro, and Photoshop.

A lifelong musician, Hamed plays multiple instruments, including guitar, bass, and oud. He is equally fascinated by smart-home technology and can happily spend hours geeking out over connected lights, speakers, sensors, and automations that make everyday life a little more interesting. When he isn’t covering the latest tech news, he explores more creative topics on his Medium blog, works on his music, or clears his head by riding his motorcycle.

Summary

  • Google’s rejected patent application describes a TV channel where an AI version of you could star in every show.
  • Your viewing habits, age group, and device location could shape what the AI makes.
  • Google could insert ads directly into the shows before they reach your screen.

Google has an idea for a constantly running TV channel where an AI-generated version of you is the star of every show. In a US patent application published on November 19, the company describes “My Channel,” a feature that would make AI-generated shows based on your viewing habits and give the lead character your face and voice.

404 Media caught this recently, and Google filed the application back in May 2025. Patentlyze reported that Google’s application had been rejected. Even if Google amends the claims and gets approval, that doesn’t necessarily mean it’s going to create the channel. However, the fact that someone actually came up with this idea is itself quite bizarre.

Google could feed the data it has on you into an AI model to write your next show

And, of course, this is all for more ads!

Based on the images filed along with the application, a TV menu with a tile labeled “My Channel” would provide you with a lineup of videos made for you. Each of these videos would have a unique title and a short description to give you an idea of what you’d be watching before you jump in. The mock-up puts a crime comedy, a romantic comedy, a sci-fi adventure, and an action thriller on the same screen. All four star the same person, a hypothetical viewer named John.

I’ll let you decide whether this sounds more like a bad version of The Truman Show or a worse Black Mirror episode. I just think Hypothetical John’s sanity will quickly deteriorate if he routinely watches nothing but his own AI-generated shows.

The AI could take cues from your favorite genres and the style of the videos you watch most. Other details, including your age group and your device’s language or location, could help shape the results. The prompt could also draw on current events. In another brilliant example, a cricket fan is watching a video that puts them in the World Cup stands and shows them cheering for India. Of course, Google! We tune in to World Cup events hoping to see ourselves.

This would require enormous amounts of computing power, but the data is already there to make super specific shows with minute details pertaining to each individual user. Google has recently allowed Gemini users to see what the AI remembers about them and make changes if necessary, although the report it gives you is far from the complete profile that Google has on you. The patent application also mentions giving users a say in when their preferences or location are collected. It leaves open how much you’d get to see of the data that shaped a particular show.

There’d be ads, too; almost the whole point of this is to show you more ads. The application describes sending a generated video to an advertising server, which could insert one or more ads before it reaches your screen. Google TV puts sponsored content alongside recommendations, and this would give Google room to sell ads inside AI-generated shows that are shaped around two important pillars: you as the star, and ad space as the driving force behind pretty much everything.
